title_en: Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Disputes over Financial Leasing Contracts

articles.content_en:
Article 1: The People's Court shall, in accordance with the provisions of Article 735 of the Civil Code, and in light of the nature and value of the subject matter, the composition of the rent, and the contractual rights and obligations of the parties, determine whether a financial leasing legal relationship is constituted.
Where a contract is named as a financial leasing contract but does not actually constitute a financial leasing legal relationship, the People's Court shall handle it in accordance with the legal relationship actually constituted.

Article 2: Where a lessee sells its own thing to the lessor and then leases the leased property back from the lessor through a financial leasing contract, the People's Court shall not determine that a financial leasing legal relationship is not constituted merely on the ground that the lessee and the seller are the same person.
II. Performance of the Contract and Publicity of the Leased Property

Article 3: Where the lessee refuses to take delivery of the leased property and fails to notify the lessor in a timely manner, or refuses to take delivery of the leased property without justifiable reasons, thereby causing losses to the lessor, and the lessor claims damages against the lessee, the People's Court shall support it.

Article 4: Where the lessor transfers part or all of its rights under the financial leasing contract, and the transferee requests dissolution or modification of the financial leasing contract on that ground, the People's Court shall not support such request.
III. Dissolution of the Contract

Article 6: Where the lessee is unable to possess or use the leased property due to the lessor's reasons, and the lessee requests dissolution of the financial leasing contract, the People's Court shall support it.

Article 7: Where a party in the first-instance litigation only requests dissolution of the financial leasing contract and does not make claims regarding the ownership of the leased property and compensation for losses, the People's Court may provide clarification to the party.
IV. Liability for Breach of Contract

Article 9: Where the lessee fails to perform the obligation to pay rent within the prescribed time limit or delays the performance of other payment obligations, and the lessor, in accordance with the provisions of the financial leasing contract, requires the lessee to pay overdue interest and corresponding liquidated damages, the People's Court shall support it.

Article 10: Where the lessor both requests the lessee to pay all the unpaid rent stipulated in the contract and requests dissolution of the financial leasing contract, the People's Court shall inform it to make a choice in accordance with the provisions of Article 752 of the Civil Code.
Where the lessor requests the lessee to pay all the unpaid rent stipulated in the contract, and after the People's Court renders a judgment the lessee fails to perform, and the lessor subsequently initiates prosecution again requesting dissolution of the financial leasing contract and recovery of the leased property, the People's Court shall accept the case.
Article 11: Where the lessor, in accordance with the provisions of Article 5 of this Interpretation, requests dissolution of the financial leasing contract and simultaneously requests recovery of the leased property and compensation for losses, the People's Court shall support it.
The scope of compensation for losses provided in the preceding paragraph is the difference between all the lessee's unpaid rent and other expenses and the value of the recovered leased property. Where the contract stipulates that after the expiration of the lease term the leased property belongs to the lessor, the scope of compensation for losses shall also include the residual value of the leased property after the expiration of the financial leasing contract.
Article 12: Where during the litigation the lessee and the lessor dispute the value of the leased property, the People's Court may determine the value of the leased property in accordance with the provisions of the financial leasing contract; if the financial leasing contract does not stipulate it or the stipulation is unclear, the value of the leased property may be determined by reference to the depreciation of the leased property stipulated in the financial leasing contract and the residual value of the leased property after the expiration of the contract.
Where the lessee or the lessor considers that the value determined in accordance with the preceding paragraph seriously deviates from the actual value of the leased property, it may request the People's Court to entrust a qualified institution to determine it through appraisal or auction.
V. Miscellaneous Provisions
Article 13: Where a dispute arises between the seller and the buyer over a sales contract, or a dispute arises between the lessor and the lessee over a financial leasing contract, and a party only initiates prosecution with respect to one of the contractual relationships, and the People's Court, after examination, considers that the party to the other contractual relationship has a legal interest in the outcome of the case, it may notify that party to participate in the litigation as a third party.
Where the lessee and the actual user of the leased property are inconsistent, and the parties to the financial leasing contract do not initiate prosecution against the actual user of the leased property, the People's Court, after examination, considers that the actual user of the leased property has a legal interest in the outcome of the case, it may notify the actual user to participate in the litigation as a third party.
Where the lessee, based on the sales contract and the financial leasing contract, directly claims against the seller the rights under the sales contract such as receiving the leased property and claiming compensation, the People's Court shall notify the lessor to participate in the litigation as a third party.
Article 14: The limitation of action for a party to request the People's Court to protect its rights due to a dispute over arrears of rent under a financial leasing contract is three years, calculated from the date of expiration of the lease term.
Article 15: This Interpretation shall come into force as of March 1, 2014. The Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Trial of Disputes over Financial Leasing Contracts (Fa Fa [1996] No. 19) shall be abolished simultaneously.
For cases of disputes over financial leasing contracts that have not yet been finally adjudicated after this Interpretation comes into force, this Interpretation shall apply; for cases that have been finally adjudicated before this Interpretation comes into force, and the parties apply for retrial or a retrial is decided in accordance with the adjudication supervision procedure, this Interpretation shall not apply.
